leave_behind.item: The 134/777 exposed-group population itself (two R-accounts genuinely sharing one situs_address in the raw WCAD source data, a real new-construction-subdivision pattern) is a structural fact about the source and is NOT resolved by this fix -- both this card and S6 correctly leave it unresolved, since there is no principled way to determine which sibling 'really' owns the numeric-roll's dollar data without a better join key WCAD itself does not expose. Both accounts now correctly carry no crosswalk-derived valueHistory row at all rather than a fabricated one.

LESSON: A disjoint copy of a fixed query does not inherit the fix -- this is the second instance of this exact failure mode in this program (S6's fix landed in parcel-record-fill.mjs's crosswalk; valueHistory's own deliberately-disjoint copy of the same query shape never received it). When a module comment says 'deliberately disjoint, keep it that way,' that is also a standing instruction to re-check that module whenever the query it's disjoint FROM gets a correctness fix, not just a performance or feature change.

A prior card's own leave_behind is worth reading and applying proactively to a NEW build that shares its shape, not just recorded as a debt. S6's leave_behind named 'hoist the county-wide window function once, don't recompute per chunk' as a self-inflicted performance regression; this card's own hoisted-guard design applied that lesson from the very first version, at zero extra cost, because it was already known.

Where a collision mechanism differs in shape from a prior card's own (S6: four independently-nullable scalar fields per account; valueHistory: one merged tuple per account per year), the ACTUALLY-COLLIDED test has to be re-derived for the new shape, not copy-pasted -- here, existence of 2+ distinct place_keys sharing a viaCrosswalk row for one group-year IS the collision (no per-field partial case), simpler than S6's own OWN_ROW_DOLLAR_FIELDS_SQL nullability check, because a crosswalk row is written all-or-nothing per year, not per field.
